summary.text: 事 began as a picture of a hand holding an unidentified object. The early graph is associated with duties, events and serving; no single path among these uses is established.

formation.text: Pictographic: early forms depict a hand holding something. The object has been identified in competing proposals as a flag, document container, brush or implement, but its identity is unresolved. A later dictionary analysis divides 事 into 史 and an abbreviated 之 used for sound; this does not establish how the early graph was formed.

components.text: The early graph is a whole picture of a hand holding an unidentified object. Competing proposals identify the object as a flag, document container, brush or implement; it is not securely identified.

history.text: Paleographic accounts describe 事, 史, 吏 and 使 as later differentiated forms of an earlier shared graph showing a hand holding something. Records list oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal and Shuowen form categories, but do not date the first individual specimen. The selected seal-script image is a modern redraw of a received form, not an ancient artifact.

The received Shuowen analysis treats 史 as the meaning element and abbreviated 之 as a sound element. This later analysis differs from the account of related graphs differentiating from a shared earlier form; the early graph’s components are not thereby established.

uncertainties.text: The held object’s identity and name remain disputed. Since its name and pronunciation are not established, a sound-based borrowing from that object’s name is not demonstrated.
The examples attest several uses but do not establish a complete chronology or a single semantic path connecting them.

senses.text: Bronze-inscription examples attest 事 for duty or office. The cited examples do not establish this use as earlier than the other attested uses.

senses.period: Bronze inscriptions and early texts; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze inscriptions attest an event sense, and cited early-text examples use 事 for matters or events. The evidence does not establish priority among these uses.

senses.period: Bronze inscriptions and early texts; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze examples attest a command or service use; cited early-text examples also attest serving and undertaking. They do not establish a linear development from duty or event.
Current uses include affair, matter and business.

limitations.text: The cited examples support multiple uses but do not establish the original spoken word’s precise meaning or a chronological chain among the attested senses.

overview.text: 事 pictures a hand holding something, whose identity is disputed. Bronze inscriptions attest uses for duty, events and serving; they do not show how these meanings developed from one another.

components.text: The whole early picture shows a hand holding an object; proposals for what it was remain disputed.
